# Sigta UI — LLM Agent Rules

> This file is published into your project by `npx sigta install`. It is the
> **single source of truth** for how an LLM coding agent should use Sigta UI.
> It is overwritten on every `sigta install` — never hand-edit it here; change
> it in the package instead. For the full component API, see
> `sigta-components.md` in the same directory.

Sigta UI is a design system with two runtimes; this project uses the
**Svelte 5** one (`@sigta-hq/svelte`). Components are Svelte components; a
dotted name is a member of its family:

```svelte
<script>
    import { Button, Dropdown } from '@sigta-hq/svelte';
</script>

<Button variant="cta">Save</Button>
<Dropdown><Dropdown.Item>Rename</Dropdown.Item></Dropdown>
```

## MUST — non-negotiable

### 1. Always use Sigta components, never raw HTML equivalents

When a Sigta component exists for an element, **use it**. Never reach for the
raw HTML tag with Tailwind utility classes.

| Want this | Use this | Never write |
|---|---|---|
| Button / link | `<Button>` | `<button class="bg-… text-… rounded-…">` |
| Text input | `<Input>` | `<input class="border …">` |
| Textarea | `<Textarea>` | `<textarea class="…">` |
| Select | `<Select>` | `<select class="…">` |
| Checkbox | `<Checkbox>` | `<input type="checkbox" class="…">` |
| Radio | `<Radio>` | `<input type="radio" class="…">` |
| Toggle | `<Switch>` | custom toggle markup |
| Range slider | `<Slider>` | `<input type="range" class="…">` |
| Field wrapper | `<Field>` | hand-rolled label/error markup |
| Icon | `<Icon name="…">` | `<svg>` / any icon library |
| Badge / status pill | `<Badge>` / `<Pill>` | `<span class="rounded-full …">` |
| Alert / status box | `<Callout>` | `<div role="alert" class="…">` |
| Modal | `<Modal>` + `<Modal.Trigger>` | custom dialog markup |
| Tooltip | `<Tooltip>` | `title=` attr or custom popover |
| Dropdown menu | `<Dropdown>` + `<Dropdown.Item>` | custom menu |
| Tabs | `<Tabs>` family | custom tab JS |
| Accordion / FAQ | `<Accordion>` + `<Accordion.Item>` | custom `<details>` styling |
| Card / surface | `<Card>` / `<Panel>` | `<div class="border rounded-…">` |
| Heading | `<Heading>` | `<h1 class="font-… text-…">` |
| Body text variant | `<Text>` | `<p class="text-…">` |
| Avatar | `<Avatar>` | `<img class="rounded-full …">` |
| Loading indicator / spinner | `<Loader>` | a spinner SVG, `animate-spin`, "Loading…" text |
| "Saving…" / "Saved" indicator | `<SaveState>` | hand-written status text, `{#if saving}` spans |
| Background job / queue progress | `<Job>` | a progress bar + text assembled by hand |
| A count that changes (unread, open) | `<Count>` | a bare `{n}` in a badge |

For the complete list with props and variants, read **`sigta-components.md`**.

### 2. Never use raw colors — tokens only

**Never** write hex (`#1a2b3c`) or Tailwind palette classes (`text-gray-500`,
`bg-blue-600`, `border-slate-200`). Use the semantic token utilities:

- **Surfaces / text:** `bg-surface`, `bg-surface-raised`, `text-ink`,
  `text-graphite`, `border-line`
- **Brand / status:** `bg-accent`, `border-accent-line`, `text-success`,
  `text-danger`, `bg-danger`
- **Inverse (dark bands):** `bg-ink`, `bg-inverse`, `text-inverse-fg`,
  `text-inverse-fg-muted`, `border-inverse-line`

When a utility doesn't exist, use the raw CSS var inline:
`max-w-(--sigta-maxw)`, `px-(--sigta-gutter)`, or `var(--sigta-*)` in an
arbitrary value. The rule is absolute: **no literal colors outside the theme
layer.**

### 3. Never import another icon library

Use `<Icon name="…">` (Lucide under the hood, one pinned set). Do not add
Heroicons, Phosphor, Feather, `lucide-svelte` or any other icon set — not even
Lucide's own package: `<Icon>` already carries the set at the brand stroke.
If a needed icon is missing from Lucide, say so in a comment rather than
substituting another library.

### 4. Foundation must be wired before components work

Install from GitHub Packages (an `.npmrc` with
`@sigta-hq:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com` and a token with
`read:packages`), then import the stylesheet once and mount the toast region
in the root layout:

```css
/* app.css — with Tailwind v4 (for the token utilities in your own markup) */
@import "tailwindcss";
@import "@sigta-hq/contract/tailwind.css";
@import "@sigta-hq/svelte/sigta.css";
```

```svelte
<!-- the root layout -->
<script>
    import { Toast } from '@sigta-hq/svelte';

    let { children } = $props();
</script>

{@render children()}
<Toast />
```

Without Tailwind, `import '@sigta-hq/svelte/sigta.css'` alone styles every
component (you lose only the token utilities for your own markup).

If any of it is missing, components render unstyled or broken. Do not try to
"fix" missing styles by adding utility classes to components — fix the
foundation. Components carry no utility classes of their own: their look lives
in the Sigta stylesheet, keyed on `data-sigta`, `data-part`, `data-variant`
and state attributes. A `class` you pass is applied on top and wins.

### 5. A loader never moves

Whatever state the work is in, the compass stays exactly where it is and
nothing around it shifts. Words popping in beside it, a percentage gaining a
digit, a loader that exists only while busy: each one makes the mark jump and
the UI feel unfinished. Work out every state before you place one:

- **Keep it rendered; change its state.** Never mount or unmount a loader, or
  the words beside it, per request: no `{#if}` or `hidden` around them. Drive
  `state` (`idle` → `working` → `done`) instead. If it must not show at rest,
  keep its box and hide it with `invisible`:
  `class={busy ? '' : 'invisible'}`.
- **Let the kit hold the space.** `<SaveState>` keeps the width of its
  longest label, `<Button>` keeps its label and stands the compass in
  for its icon only once an action outlasts a beat, `<Job>` gives its
  percentage a fixed width. Reach for them before pairing a loader with text
  by hand, and never swap a button's label for "Saving…" or for the loader.
- **Pin the compass to the side that stays put; the words grow away from
  it.** Against a right edge (the end of a toolbar, a `justify-between`
  header, the last table cell) use `<SaveState>` with `align="end"`, or put a
  hand-built loader after its text and right-align the text. Anything between
  the loader and the edge it hangs from will push it. In a centred group both
  ends move, so reserve the words' room (next rule).
- **Reserve room for words and numbers that change.** Stack the alternatives
  in one grid cell (`grid` on the wrapper, `[grid-area:1/1]` on each label,
  `invisible` on all but the current one), or give the text a fixed width.
  Numbers get `tabular-nums` and a width that fits their longest value
  (`w-[4ch] text-right` for a percentage). Reserve the height too when a
  label changes font (`min-h-*`).
- **Hold the place of what is loading.** A loader standing in for content sits
  in a slot as tall as that content will be (`min-h-*`), so the content
  arriving doesn't shove the page.

```svelte
<!-- Never: right-aligned, so "Saved" appearing after the compass pushes it left -->
<header class="flex items-center justify-between">
    <Heading>Draft</Heading>
    <span class="flex items-center gap-2">
        {#if saving}<Loader size="sm" />{/if}
        {#if saved}<span>Saved</span>{/if}
    </span>
</header>

<!-- Instead: the compass sits flush right and never moves; its words grow leftward -->
<header class="flex items-center justify-between">
    <Heading>Draft</Heading>
    <SaveState state={saveState} idle="All changes saved" align="end" />
</header>

<!-- By hand: the loader keeps its box and both labels share one cell -->
<span class="inline-flex items-center gap-2">
    <Loader size="sm" decorative class={syncing ? '' : 'invisible'} />
    <span role="status" class="grid">
        <span class="[grid-area:1/1] {syncing ? 'invisible' : ''}">Synced</span>
        <span class="[grid-area:1/1] {syncing ? '' : 'invisible'}">Syncing with the bank</span>
    </span>
</span>
```

## SHOULD — strong defaults

### Fonts and type roles

- Headings: `font-head` (Fraunces). Body prose: `font-body` (Newsreader).
- UI chrome (labels, buttons, nav, table headers, badges):
  `font-mono` (JetBrains Mono), small sizes (0.62–0.82rem), letter-spacing
  0.04–0.22em, often uppercase.
- Decorative handwriting: `font-hand` (Caveat) — sparingly.

### Shape and depth

- Controls: `rounded-base` (3px). Cards/panels: `rounded-panel` (6px).
  Devices/spotlights: `rounded-frame` (10px).
- Card elevation: `shadow-paper`. Hover lift on actionable cards:
  `hover:-translate-y-[2px]` + the shadow.

### Brand voice

- Accent (highlighter yellow) is **scarce**: one mark per view, status
  highlights only. Never large accent fills.
- Borders: strong outline `border-[1.5px] border-ink`; hairline `border border-line`.
- Numbers in data contexts: `tabular-nums`.
- Hand-drawn flourishes (rules, sparklines): `<Rule>`, `<Annot>`,
  `<Chart.Sparkline>` — inline SVG with `currentColor`.

### Motion — finishing things should feel finished

- **Never show "Loading…" / "Saving…" text or a generic spinner.** Use
  `<Loader>` (the Sigta compass), `<SaveState>` for saves, `<Job>` for
  long-running work. A `<Button loading={form.processing}>` already shows the
  compass beside its label when its action runs long, and nothing for a quick
  one: don't add text or a loader to it. Wherever a loader goes, it holds
  still (MUST 5).
- **Completing an item must not just make it vanish.** Put list rows in a
  `data-sigta-motion` container, key the `{#each}` and give each row
  `out:leave` (`import { leave } from '@sigta-hq/svelte'`), wrap the title's
  text in `<span data-sigta-strike>`, and complete through
  `sigta.complete(event.currentTarget, () => remove(item))`: it ticks,
  crosses out and folds the row away, and restores it if the commit fails.
  Offer Undo with `sigta.toast({ …, action: { text: 'Undo', onClick }, key: '…' })`.
- **Celebrate sparingly.** `sigta.celebrate(el, 'small')` for a satisfying
  tick; `'big'` (confetti) only for milestones like inbox zero or a finished
  import.
- **Don't hand-roll keyframes or easing.** Use `animate-sigta-settle`,
  `ease-sigta-out` / `ease-sigta-pen` / `ease-sigta-spring` and the
  `--sigta-dur-*` tokens. Reduced motion is handled by the kit; never make an
  animation the only carrier of meaning.

## Component prop conventions

Prop names, variant values and slot names are shared by every Sigta runtime:
`variant`, `size`, `icon`, `label`, `description`, `error`,
`placeholder`, `heading`, `name`, `href`. Multi-word props are camelCase
(`primaryLabel`). Two-way state uses `bind:` (`bind:value`, `bind:checked`,
`bind:open`); events are callback props (`onchange`, `onmove`, `onsubmit`);
named slots are snippets of the same name (`{#snippet footer()}…{/snippet}`).
Attributes you don't recognize (`name`, `id`, `aria-*`, `data-*`) **forward
onto the native element**.

## Cross-component events

Some components communicate via window events. Listen for / dispatch these
rather than building custom wiring:

- `sigta-toast` `{heading, text, variant, duration, link, action, key}` → shows a toast (`<Toast />` mounted once). Prefer `sigta.toast()` (`import { sigta } from '@sigta-hq/svelte'`) or `window.Sigta.toast()`.
- `sigta-celebrate` `{level, text, target}` → a burst / ring + note / paper confetti. Prefer `sigta.celebrate(el, level)`.
- `sigta-save-state` `{name, state}` → drives the `<SaveState name="…">` with that name. Prefer `sigta.save(promise, name)`.
- `sigta-modal-show` / `sigta-modal-hide` `{name}` → open/close a modal by name (or use `bind:open`).
- Component events are callback props: `<Composer onsubmit>`, `<Kanban onmove>`.

## Svelte notes

Components work in plain Svelte 5 and SvelteKit, and render on the server.
Behavior that is not Svelte state — motion, toasts, celebrations — lives in
the shared Sigta core and installs itself on the client the first time a
component mounts (`ensureRuntime()` from `@sigta-hq/svelte` does it
explicitly).

### Toast API

Trigger a toast with `sigta.toast('msg')` or `window.Sigta.toast(...)`.
Variants include `warning` and `info`. Mount `<Toast />` once in your root
layout.

### Inertia (any backend)

With Inertia, `@sigta-hq/svelte/inertia` turns a `sigta` page prop into
toasts and celebrations, so any backend (Laravel, Go, …) can raise them:

```json
{ "sigta": { "toasts": [{ "text": "Saved", "variant": "success" }], "celebrate": { "level": "small" } } }
```

```js
// app.js — after createInertiaApp
import { connectInertia } from '@sigta-hq/svelte/inertia';
connectInertia();
```

`connectInertia({ saveState: 'page' })` also drives `<SaveState name="page">`
from every non-GET visit: saving, then saved, or failed on validation errors.

### Language

Sigta's own strings (aria labels such as "Toggle navigation", empty states
such as "No people found.") are English until you give the root layout a
message map keyed by the English text — the same shape as a Laravel
`lang/<locale>.json`, so a backend's translation file works as is:

```svelte
<script>
    import { setMessages } from '@sigta-hq/svelte';
    import da from '../lang/da.json';
    let { children } = $props();
    setMessages(da);
</script>

{@render children()}
```

It lives in Svelte context, so server renders in different languages never
mix. Never hard-code a translation into a Sigta component's label prop to work
around a missing message — add the message.

## When to extend vs. when to ask

If the design calls for something no Sigta component covers, **prefer composing
existing components** (a `<Card>` containing a `<Button>` + a
`<Badge>`) over writing bespoke markup. If composition can't satisfy the
need, leave a clear comment saying what's missing and why — do not silently
introduce a parallel component vocabulary.
